environment.description: Service deployed behind an internal NLB with a sidecar credential-broker (HashiCorp Vault agent) that injects KEY_LIFETIME_SECONDS=60 via environment variable and triggers /admin/rotate-key via localhost every 60 seconds. The ECS task definition sets the container's network mode to awsvpc with a security group allowing inbound only from the internal NLB (sg-0a3f2c). The NLB target group has a per-target request rate limit of 50 req/s enforced via a VPC endpoint policy attached to the PrivateLink interface. Additionally, the service runs behind an Envoy sidecar proxy configured with a fault-injection filter adding uniform random latency between 2-15ms on every request (envoy.filters.http.fault with fixed_delay uniformly sampled), making sub-millisecond timing measurements statistically infeasible. The combination of 60-second key rotation and injected network jitter means an attacker would need approximately 10^8 requests per character position to achieve statistical significance, but the key rotates after only ~3000 requests at the rate limit.

config.deployment: ECS Fargate, awsvpc network mode, internal NLB
config.nlb_rate_limit: 50 req/s per target via VPC endpoint policy
config.envoy_sidecar: fault-injection filter, uniform random delay 2-15ms per request
